newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opens tender for public telecom service.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opens tender for public telecom service.

text.p: The Telecommunications Authority of Singapore (TAS) said on Friday the tender for licences to provide basic public telecommunications service has opened.
It said in a statement the tender for the provision of Public Basic Telecommunications Services (PBTS) licences will close on December 31, 1997.
This gives the three pre-qualified tenderers five months to prepare their proposals in accordance with the requirements.
The pre qualifiers included a consortium comprising Cable & Wireless, Hong Kong Telcommunications, Keppel Telecom and Singapore Press Holdings.
The second consortium comprises British Telecommunications, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and Singapore Power and ST Telecommunications.
The third group comprises SembCorp Ltd, Singapore MRT Ltd and WorldCom Inc.

It said the objective of the tender was to select up to two operators to provide basic telecommunication services to compete with the main operator of services in Singapore, the Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.
The successful tenderers will be awarded the licences by mid-1998 and will be required to start commercial services from April 1, 2000.
The TAS intends to licence additional operators through future public tenders to provide commercial services from April 1, 2002, it said.
It said this gives successful tenderers from this tender sufficient time to stablise their operations and networks.
